title: Sissle asks him to rebuild the Ambassador band; he chooses Chez Florence
summary: Sissle, back in Paris with a USO show, asked Briggs to reform an orchestra for the Ambassador, but Briggs thought the large room too risky and preferred Chez Florence.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, what else have we got to --
Yes, now after the war then, you went to Chez Florence; is that right?

Yes, after the war, we organized an orchestra. We had a proposition for Chez Florence, which I appreciated, 'cause many of my friends, tried to get the same proposition, which was about the best thing that was offered for the time being.

Noble Sissle came back to Paris, in a U.S.O. show, and he tried to get me to reform his orchestra for him, in Paris, to reopen the Ambassadors, for Mr. Fischer. Latiege & Fischer, who had it before with Mr. Sayag. They had decided to take over, Latiege & Fischer, the booking office.
And Noble asked me to get musicians for him and to form an orchestra for him.
But, there was something that worried me, ever so much. I said, "The Ambassadors is a great big place, and the war is just finished. It will take time for
the select people to come back. They must be sure there's no personal danger before they come back. (Laughter).
For my own personal reasons, you see, I said, 'I think I'll take Chez Florence's.'
